No evidence found of credential theft, malicious reconnaissance, data exfiltration, or prompt injection in the two reviewed files.

content.user_title: Run Local Models on Apple Silicon with mlx-optiq
content.value_statement: Local model serving requires matching model size, memory limits, and client settings. This skill guides mlx-optiq checks, consent-based server startup, client connections, and performance evaluation.
actual_capabilities: Check Mac architecture, installed memory, Python version, and mlx-optiq availability using read-only commands.
Guide quantized model selection using catalog identifiers and memory headroom.
Start a localhost model server after user confirmation and explain authentication requirements for network access.
Smoke-test chat completions and explain client base URL, model label, and authentication settings.
Guide repeated timing tests, task-specific quality checks, local evaluation, and throughput prediction.
Explain context limits, concurrency, idle unloading, cache quantization, and disk-streaming tradeoffs.
limitations: Targets Apple Silicon Macs, not Intel Macs, Windows, or hosted-model selection.
Requires separately installed mlx-optiq and Python 3.11 or newer; the skill does not install software.
Initial model downloads require user approval and can consume several gigabytes.
Memory estimates are approximate; long context, quantization, and disk streaming can reduce performance or answer quality.

prompt_templates.title: Check local readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my Mac can run mlx-optiq using read-only commands. Show the results without installing software, downloading models, or starting a server.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: verify architecture, memory, Python, and tool availability.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a model
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a quantized model for my Mac using available memory and the mlx-optiq catalog. Explain headroom and ask before any download.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: select a model after prerequisite checks.

prompt_templates.title: Serve and connect
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a localhost mlx-optiq server and client smoke test. Confirm the model identifier, explain authentication settings, and request approval before startup or downloads.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: connect a client to local inference.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate memory and performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Design repeated short and long prompt tests for my local model. Compare context, concurrency, and cache settings, checking answer quality separately from speed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate tuning choices under memory constraints.

output_examples.input: What should I verify before running a model locally?
output: Confirm Apple Silicon architecture, installed memory, Python 3.11 or newer, and an available optiq command.
Choose model weights comfortably below total memory, leaving space for the cache, macOS, and other applications.
Request approval before downloading model files or starting the server.

output_examples.input: My local model server runs out of memory. What should I change?
output: Try a smaller model, reduce concurrent requests, and lower the context limit.
Consider cache quantization only when memory savings are needed; measure its effect on speed.
Repeat representative prompts and verify answer quality after changing settings.

output_examples.input: How should I configure a client for localhost inference?
output: Use http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 as the client base URL when the server uses the example port.
Use the served repository identifier as the model label to avoid client confusion.
Do not reuse a cloud API secret; follow the local server's token requirements and supply its configured key when required.

best_practices: Keep serving on loopback unless network access is intentional; require an API key before binding to another host.
Reserve memory for model weights, cache, macOS, and other applications; use conservative context and concurrency limits.
Obtain approval before downloads or startup, and compare repeated timing measurements with independently checked answer quality.
anti_patterns: Starting a server or downloading several gigabytes without user approval.
Assuming model weights alone determine memory use or that advertised context always fits.
Treating faster decoding or cache quantization as proof of better answer quality.

faq.question: Which computers does this skill support?
faq.answer: It targets Apple Silicon Macs. Intel Macs, Windows, and hosted-model advice are outside its scope.

faq.question: Does this skill install mlx-optiq?
faq.answer: No. It checks availability and directs you to installation documentation when needed. You must install mlx-optiq separately with Python 3.11 or newer.

faq.question: Will starting the server download a model?
faq.answer: The first startup downloads the selected model when needed. The skill requires confirmation because model downloads can consume several gigabytes.

faq.question: Do local clients need a real cloud API key?
faq.answer: No cloud key is needed. Default authentication permits missing headers, but supplied Bearer tokens must use the documented prefix; explicitly configured keys are required.

faq.question: Can other machines connect to the server?
faq.answer: Only with an appropriate network binding. The skill recommends localhost and requires an API key when serving beyond loopback.

faq.question: Does cache quantization always make inference faster?
faq.answer: No. It saves memory but can slow decoding. Measure your model and verify answer quality before adopting new settings.
